Here is the caption to process:
[Fire @ Blk 103B, Depot Road]Earlier today at about 5:30pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a twelve-floor unit.The fire, which involved one of the rooms within the unit, was extinguished with two water jets. No one was inside the unit.As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage. About 70 persons were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.A person from the affected unit who had evacuated before SCDFs arrival was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital after feeling unwell.The cause of the fire is under investigation.The top causes of fires in residential premises are unattended cooking, electrical faults, and unattended lighted materials. To prevent such fires, residents are strongly advised not to leave cooking unattended, and to avoid overloading power sockets or charging devices overnight without supervision. They should also ensure that lighted materials such as incense or cigarettes are never left unattended, and are fully extinguished before disposal.

Here is the caption to process:
[Punggol Marine Fire Post Groundbreaking Ceremony]The groundbreaking ceremony for SCDFs new Punggol Marine Fire Post (PMFP) was held earlier today (16 Jan). Mr Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry, graced the event as the Guest of Honour.The integrated land-and-sea PMFP marks a significant milestone in strengthening SCDFs emergency response capabilities in the Northeast region of Singapore. Housing a suite of land and sea-based emergency assets, the PMFP will improve response time and strengthen land-based coverage for residents in Northshore, whilst extending marine-based coverage across the entire East Johor Straits within 45 minutes.Slated for completion in end 2027, the PMFP will address evolving emergency response needs as the Punggol region continues to undergo rapid development, with new residential precincts, transport infrastructure, major developments, and maritime activities in the East Johor Straits.In line with SCDFs commitment to environmental sustainability, the PMFP will also incorporate energy-efficient and water-saving features, including solar photovoltaic panels to reduce energy consumption, and water-efficient fittings and systems to minimise water usage. It has also been designed with community-friendly features to complement the recreational and lifestyle landscape of the Punggol Northshore district.Developed in close partnership with , part of , the PMFP will feature shared usage of jetty infrastructure and facilities to optimise the utilisation of land and sea space.With todays groundbreaking ceremony, this milestone underscores SCDFs continued commitment to strengthening both land and marine emergency response, contributing to a safer and more resilient community in the Northeast region of Singapore. [34th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 41 officer cadets from the 34th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Amongst the graduating cohort were seven cadets from the Ministry of Interior, Kingdom of Bahrain and two cadets from the Vietnam Police Department of Fire & Rescue.These cadets have undergone a comprehensive seven-month training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. As Senior Officers, they will lead their fellow officers to advance the lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property.In his speech, the guest of honour, Mr Goh Pei Ming, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development, encouraged the newly commissioned cadets to lead their teams with conviction and uphold high standards in their work, while carrying out their duties with pride and care.During the event, five Officer Cadets were presented with awards to recognise their achievements in the following categories:- Overall Best Trainee: OCT Muhamad Hail Aryyan Bin Muhamad Abdullah- Best in Practical: OCT Mohd Hafizz Bin Mohd Akebal- Best in Knowledge: OCT Phone Min Myat- Best in Physical Training: OCT Seth Kho Yao-En- Best Performing International Cadet: OCT Nguyen Chi CuongCongratulations to the 34th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their lifesaving journey. ANationOfLifesavers

Yesterday, Mr Koh Soon Kiong, Coordinating Director, Jurong Lake Gardens Operations, National Parks Board, presented one of these repurposed benches to COL Dennis Quah, Commander, 4th SCDF Division, symbolising the meaningful collaboration between NParks and SCDF. This initiative reaffirms SCDFs commitment to environmental sustainability, following similar past donations made to organisations such as SPCA Singapore and Mandai Wildlife Reserve. SCDF will continue to embrace sustainability in our work and explore innovative ways to contribute to a greener, eco-friendly future.

[Illegal Fuel Dispensing is a Fire Safety Offence ] Under the Fire Safety Act, it is an offence to dispense fuel at any premises without a valid Petroleum & Flammable Materials (P&FM) storage licence. Offenders face fines of up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 6 months. In 2024, SCDF took enforcement action against three persons for illegal fuel dispensing at vehicle carparks along Alexandra Road, Chin Bee Crescent, and Eunos Road 7. The three offenders were fined between $2,800 and $3,100. In 2025 to date, enforcement action has been taken against one person. The offender was caught illegally dispensing fuel from an intermediate bulk container stored in a minivan at the junction of Tampines North Drive 4 and Tampines North Drive 5 (see attached infographic). The offender was charged in court and fined $3,000 in August 2025. SCDF takes a serious view of such fire safety offences and will not hesitate to act against offenders. Members of the public can report any illegal dispensing activities through the SCDF hotline at 1800-280-0000, the feedback form at or the myResponder app.
